text.insert: The Discord archive preserves community and developer conversations as evidence for proposed knowledge. It is a source archive, not a worker-searchable corpus: published learnings retain message-level references back to the conversation record.

text.insert: Every sync asks the mirror to refresh, then plans batches from archive lines beyond the highest ingested line for each channel and month. The refresh is best effort, so intake continues from the on-disk archive when the pull fails. Observation freezes each planned batch before the librarian validates its learnings and appends accepted records to the knowledge ledger. The sync path and `kg-librarian-backfill --source discord` share one manifest of completed and failed batches, which lets bulk historical passes resume the same work without processing accepted messages twice.
A Discord message can support a proposed learning, but the archive does not publish knowledge by itself. Classification, extraction, validation, corroboration, and publication are governed by

Workers do not search the Discord archive directly. They encounter Discord only through evidence references attached to knowledge records, which keeps conversation context available without treating unvalidated chat as operational truth.
